content: Clalit is one of Israel's leading Health Maintenance Organizations (HMOs). It was established in 1911 by a group of 150 immigrants who sought to create a mutual aid healthcare association. When the State of Israel was founded in 1948, Clalit played a significant role in restructuring the country's healthcare system to accommodate the large influx of new immigrants. Today, Clalit operates clinics in nearly every neighborhood across Israel. In January 1995, Israel implemented its national health insurance law, which established a mandatory healthcare system based on four service providers: Clalit, Leumit, Maccabi, and Meuhedet. Clalit currently insures approximately 8 million members, representing 60% of Israel's population. The organization manages its own network of hospitals throughout the country, including 14 hospitals, some of which are psychiatric and rehabilitation facilities. All of these hospitals are affiliated with universities. Additionally, Clalit operates 1,200 primary and specialized clinics, as well as a network of pharmacies and dental clinics. Clalit-Run Hospitals Rabin Medical Center – Beilinson Campus (founded in 1938) in Petah Tikva specializes in open-heart surgery, neurosurgery, and organ transplants, including heart, liver, and kidney transplants. Rabin Medical Center – Golda Campus (founded in 1942) in Petah Tikva focuses on total joint replacement, home dialysis, vascular surgery, and hematology research utilizing electron microscopy techniques. Lady Davis Hospital (founded in 1967) in Haifa is part of the modern Carmel Medical Center. It provides comprehensive healthcare to the diverse population of Haifa, its suburbs, and northern regions. Its specialties include cardiology, cardiovascular and thoracic surgery, and community medicine epidemiology. HaEmek Hospital (founded in 1930) in Afula is part of the HaEmek Valley Medical Center and specializes in treating fertility and reproductive issues. Meir Hospital (founded in 1960) in Kfar Saba is part of the Sapir Medical Center and is known for its expertise in pulmonary diseases and spinal surgery. Kaplan Medical Center (founded in 1953) in Rehovot is renowned for its expertise in hand surgery. Soroka Hospital (founded in 1960) in Beersheba is the primary hospital serving the Negev region. Yoseftal Hospital (founded in 1968) in Eilat is part of the Yoseftal Medical Center and is Israel's southernmost hospital. Criticism of Clalit-Run Hospitals In March 2007, Professor Gabi Barabash, the director of Tel Aviv's Ichilov Hospital, criticized the Israeli Health Ministry for permitting Clalit to operate private hospitals. He argued that this could have disastrous consequences for the public hospitalization system. Ruth Ralbag, a senior official in the Health Ministry's budget department, contended that the incentives for establishing private hospitals contribute to the decline of the public health system and exacerbate the division of healthcare access between wealthy and poor populations.
